segments.text: In this town, when someone dies, they get one more day. We call it the Visit.
They come back at sunrise, and they leave at sunset. They eat, they laugh, they hug you, just like before.
But visitors don't show up in mirrors. Their footprints melt right out of the snow. And they never remember how they died.
And there's one rule. You never tell a visitor they're dead. If they figure it out, they vanish on the spot. No goodbye.
So on visit days, families cover every mirror, hide the newspaper, and smile way too much.
I'm twelve. My little sister Lily is seven. Last winter, Lily fell through the ice on Miller Pond.
This morning, every mirror in our house was covered with a bedsheet. Dad called in sick. Mom made chocolate chip pancakes. Nobody had made those since the pond.
So I knew today was Lily's visit. And I swore she would never find out.
I hid the newspaper. I unplugged the TV. When she asked why Mom was crying, I said onions.
All day, Lily wouldn't let go of my hand. Outside, she walked behind me, stepping in my footprints, like she used to.
Our dog Biscuit hid under the porch and whimpered every time we came close. And Dad kept staring at us, like he was trying to memorize a face.
At four o'clock, Lily let go of my hand and ran straight toward Miller Pond. I chased her through the snow, screaming her name. If she saw that pond, she would remember. And she would be gone.
She stopped right at the edge, crying.
This is where you saved me. You pushed me up onto the ice... but you didn't come back up.
I looked down at the frozen pond. Lily's reflection was there, crying. Next to her was nobody.
I looked behind us. One set of footprints. Small ones. Lily wasn't stepping in my footprints. She was making them for me.
The mirrors. The pancakes. Dad memorizing a face. It was never Lily's visit. It was mine.
Why did you tell me, I whispered. Now I'll vanish.
She wiped her nose on her mitten.
The sun's going down anyway. And I never got to say thank you.
So I hugged her as hard as I could. Stay off the ice, I said. Forever. She laughed and cried at the same time.
Then the sun went down, and Lily walked home in her own footprints.
Would you want one more day, if it was yours?
